definition.value: Detective controls are designed to search for and identify errors or undesirable events after they have occurred so that corrective actions can be taken.

definition.value: Directive controls give direction. These can be, for example, statutory obligations, regulatory standards including professional standards, or other organisational requirements or instructions, many of which are converted into policies, procedures, circulars, standard operating procedures and training.

definition.value: An ISO control is defined as a measure that modifies or maintains risk. Some of the controls in this document are controls that modify risk, while others maintain risk. An information security policy, for example, can only maintain risk, whereas compliance with the information security policy can modify risk.  Moreover, some controls describe the same generic measure in different risk contexts. This document provides a generic mixture of organizational, people, physical and technological information security controls derived from internationally recognized best practices.

comment.en: An ISO control is defined as a measure that modifies or maintains risk. Some of the controls in this document are controls that modify risk, while others maintain risk. An information security policy, for example, can only maintain risk, whereas compliance with the information security policy can modify risk.  Moreover, some controls describe the same generic measure in different risk contexts. This document provides a generic mixture of organizational, people, physical and technological information security controls derived from internationally recognized best practices.

definition.value: Actions are a future measure that will maintain and/or modify a risk. In the HSE, an action is a future measure to further reduce either the likelihood or impact of a risk.

definition.value: Preventative controls are controls designed to stop, discourage, pre-empt or limit the possibility of an undesirable event before it occurs.

definition.value: Controls are measures that maintain and/or modify risk. In the HSE, a control is a measure that is in place, is working effectively and operating to reduce either the likelihood or impact of a risk.

comment.en: Controls are measures that maintain and/or modify risk. In the HSE, a control is a measure that is in place, is working effectively and operating to reduce either the likelihood or impact of a risk.
